ov: One of the first animals ever domesticated, from the wild goat in Iran about 10,000 years ago. Kept for milk, meat, hair and skins, there were more than 1.1 billion goats in 2022.

why.p: Mostly livestock, but some people keep goats as pets for the close bonds they form.
why.et: About 440 million goats are slaughtered for meat each year worldwide.

wt: 20–27 kg (small does) to over 140 kg (Boer bucks)
rg: Farmed worldwide. Goats easily go feral, and wild herds live in Australia, New Zealand, Great Britain and elsewhere.
df: Browsers rather than grazers: goats eat leaves, shrubs and woody plants as well as grass.

cf.tip: A goat usually has a beard and holds its short tail up. A sheep’s tail hangs down, even when short, and its upper lip is split.

fx: Both male and female goats can grow beards.
